Lab 02 in seven animated steps

Each picture shows one step of the lab with the fictional "Team Menu" of the Class 3 lecture. The full instructions are in the lab; the rules are in the Conditions document. Replay any step, or download it.

Tools and techniques are open. Everything named here is a starting point, never a rule: use any suitable, available tool — or create your own. Research a tool thoroughly before adopting it (official site, free-tier limits, terms of use, a link check with VirusTotal).

The 3 hours of Lab 02

  • 1 · 2 · 1: the lecture hour is the input; the lab is 2 h Team Studio (CQ1 (Checkpoint Quiz 1) first, then Planning, Build, Review, Retro) + 1 h Home Sprint.
  • Lab work ≈ 165 minutes — under the 3-hour cap. Nothing new starts at home.
  • Feedback date: Sunday, October 11, 23:59 (written feedback + your Mid-Term desk). Final deadline for all labs: Sunday, December 20, 2026, 23:59.

Step 1 · Roles roulette and rotation table (20')

  • Draw the member order fairly — slips in a cup, a die, a list randomizer, a spreadsheet — or a method you invent.
  • Round-robin: at each Team Studio the list turns by one; the Product Owner is the next name, the Scrum Master the name after.
  • Check the two rules for Oct 12 → Nov 2: each member Product Owner once and Scrum Master once; never both in one row.

Step 2 · Three role cards (30')

  • Five lines per card: accountable for · three responsibilities (verbs) · decides · does not decide · one anti-pattern and its visible sign.
  • Four minutes silent writing, five minutes merging, one minute boundary test per card.
  • Boundary test: the same decision never appears on two cards — only the Sprint Goal belongs to the whole Scrum Team.

Step 3 · Empiricism plan and values pledge (20')

  • One line each for transparency (what, where, to whom), inspection (when, what, who) and adaptation (who changes what, how fast).
  • An acceptable limit with a number — without it, inspection cannot tell a deviation from normal variation.
  • Five value behaviours — commitment, focus, openness, respect, courage — each one could be filmed.

Step 4 · Cross-functional check and team size (10')

  • Rate 0 / 1 / 2 per member and skill; the team's level is the best in the row (the test is for the team, not each person).
  • Every gap gets a plan line: pairing, an official tutorial, a swap of tasks, or a smaller scope.
  • Communication paths = n × (n − 1) ÷ 2: 6 for four people, 45 for ten.

Home Sprint · Step 5 · Scrum history timeline (25')

  • Five to seven milestones — at least 1986, 1995, 2001, 2010, 2020.
  • Each: year · name · one sentence of at most 30 words in your own words · one https:// source you opened.
  • Check every link before you click it (VirusTotal, Google Safe Browsing).

Home Sprint · Steps 6–8 · Polish, check, submit (35')

  • Four checks: fair rotation · no decision with two owners · a numeric limit · every timeline line sourced. Then one cold read.
  • Three pages at most; footer complete. File: DIG123_D3_<TeamName>_<date>.pdf; each member submits it with their own Learning Log.
  • Improve and resubmit after the feedback; the last version submitted by December 20, 23:59 is graded.
Note on versions. These animations are self-made diagrams of the lab's steps; they show no third-party software. Any website, tool or service mentioned in the lab may have changed after October 2026 or may have a newer version — look for the same words and the same action, and check the official site.
